desc:
You are given closed intervals intervals[i] = [left, right] and a list of integer queries. The size of an interval is right - left + 1.

For every query q, find the smallest size among the intervals that contain q (that is, left ≤ q ≤ right). If no interval contains q, the answer for that query is -1. Return the answers in the order of the queries.

intervals = [[1,4],[2,4],[3,6],[4,4]], queries = [2,3,4,5,9]
q=2: [1,4] (4), [2,4] (3) -> 3
q=3: [1,4], [2,4], [3,6] -> sizes 4, 3, 4 -> 3
q=4: [4,4] has size 1 -> 1
q=5: only [3,6] (4) -> 4
q=9: none -> -1
answer = [3, 3, 1, 4, -1]
hints: Checking every interval for every query is O(nq). The queries are independent, so you may answer them in any order you like.
Answer the queries in increasing order. Then an interval becomes relevant once left ≤ q, and it is useless forever after right < q.

Sort intervals by left and queries ascending (remember their original positions). Push intervals with left ≤ q into a min-heap of (size, right). Pop from the top while right < q; the top, if any, is the answer.
editorial: Offline processing turns a 2-D condition into a sweep. When queries are sorted ascending, the set of intervals with left ≤ q only grows, so each interval is inserted exactly once with a single pointer into the sorted interval list.

Among the inserted intervals we want the smallest size whose right end is at least q. Intervals with right < q can be discarded permanently, since later queries are larger. We discard lazily: a min-heap ordered by size exposes the best candidate, and while its right end is smaller than q we pop it. Whatever is left on top contains q (it started at or before q and ends at or after q) and has the minimum size.
Sorting costs O((n + q) log) and each interval is pushed and popped at most once, so the total is O((n + q) log n) time and O(n + q) space.
solution:
import heapq


def minInterval(intervals, queries):
    iv = sorted(intervals)
    order = sorted(range(len(queries)), key=lambda i: queries[i])
    res = [-1] * len(queries)
    h = []
    p = 0
    for qi in order:
        q = queries[qi]
        while p < len(iv) and iv[p][0] <= q:
            heapq.heappush(h, (iv[p][1] - iv[p][0] + 1, iv[p][1]))
            p += 1
        while h and h[0][1] < q:
            heapq.heappop(h)
        if h:
            res[qi] = h[0][0]
    return res
